- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged 3–5 day average.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.10) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for suppressed volatility.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–5 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative — adjust downward bias by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is flat or negative over last 7 days.
- If sentiment spikes to 0.40+ and price is trending up, model may overreact — cap forecast at 10–15% below 30-day true mean to avoid overfitting.
